# Visible Medicine completion checklist

Revision 42 · Updated 2026-10-17

Track the full website and Atlas roadmap, owner clinical inputs and optional product ideas without equating drafts or tests with clinical completion.

This is the persistent project checklist, not a claim that the whole website is finished. The JSON companion is the editable status register; regenerate this view with `node scripts/refresh-completion-checklist.mjs` and verify with `--check --verify-evidence`.

## Current baseline

Atlas source: `0ac11ca2eb8effe47f2b6927f7987a9a36c7e3a2`. Website HEAD: `b953ff3f5f1891599cb6e91cb91311d9d6006270` with preserved unpublished changes. Review binding: `301707213f9c79bc07eb091870c616bf5f1d413511e19a7e1a2457c9db4581a6`.

1104 root-body representations have 9936 topic placements: 9314 editorial drafts, 583 pending and 39 generated identification prompts. Separate scopes include 108 nested selections, 51 regional tours / 309 stops and 9 independent guides / 73 stops.

Overlapping source representations and topic placements, not unique lessons, complete anatomy, acquired-image coverage, private approval counts or a completion percentage. Private clinical decisions were not read. Atlas resource registry counts do not measure the separate website's native CT/MRI integration.

Integrated Atlas source: `0ac11ca2eb8effe47f2b6927f7987a9a36c7e3a2` (9314 draft / 583 pending / 39 generated topic placements). **Imported into the website baseline above.** Atlas source and four learner runtimes remain at the installed0ac11ca2 source, with unchanged anatomy and teaching counts. The compact head comparison toolbar has a new exact website-renderer/Review binding. No source, model, scan, mask, readiness or approval promotion. Clinical, acquired-image, hosted-auth/D1, keyboard/browser and public-release acceptance remain independently scoped.

Canonical Atlas summaries were refreshed and verified through their generator (BASE-02). Source-candidate evidence remains separate from the website baseline and from clinical, browser and release approval.

## How to track progress

- Stable IDs survive reordering. Split an item into linked child IDs when necessary; do not silently delete scope.
- Update status, exact source/revision, evidence and dated change log after each verified milestone.
- Recheck stale evidence after a relevant source, renderer, case or contract change; never migrate approval automatically.
- Report counts by status, owner and area; optional ideas are separate. Do not calculate an overall completion percentage from unequal items.
- An owner-gated item does not stop independent engineering, teaching drafts or review preparation.
- No patient data, private review notes, images, identifiers, credentials or uncleared derivatives belong in this checklist or GitHub.
- Public deployment, billing, permissions, privacy clearance and clinical sign-off require their own authorization and evidence.

A checked item means its **bounded local implementation or inventory criterion** is verified. It does not mean clinical sign-off, physical-device acceptance or public release. Those have their own rows. A held or owner-gated item is not a project-wide stop.

## Recommended order

1. Confirm the intended first release scope and learners (BASE-03), and freeze a review candidate (BASE-04). Continue independent development in parallel.
2. Repair complete-suite release assurance (REL-01), complete real desktop/accessibility journeys (UX-01–03), and verify native CT/MRI plus protected Education delivery (IMG-01–02).
3. Review the included anatomy and teaching in the private Clinical Review inbox (ANAT-18, TEACH-10); work through source holds and evidence-backed content gaps in coherent regional batches.
4. Finish the selected course/exam and operational release gates. Add optional ideas only when they improve an agreed learner/author task and do not clutter the UI.

## Your next inputs

- Choose the initial audience, regions/modalities and courses; the full roadmap remains intact even if the first private beta is bounded.
- Use [Clinical Review inbox](http://127.0.0.1:3000/workspace/clinical-review-inbox) to review exact model/teaching/head packages. Record corrections and source-bound decisions, not blanket approval.
- Adjudicate held anatomy only within appropriate expertise; nominate specialist help where needed.
- Identify the intended cleared cases, presentation source files and lecture anchors. Local use approval does not itself authorize upload.
- Later, approve the real deployment target, governance/contact details, operational ownership and any commercial activation.

## My continuing work

I can inventory sources and gaps, research acceptable references/assets, write review-ready teaching, prepare review packets, implement/test software and maintain this register. I cannot manufacture missing anatomy, clinical approval, registration, rights/privacy clearance, real account authority or permission to publish. Owner-gated items will not prevent independent useful work.
